https://www.politico.eu/article/police-p.text: PARIS — A wave of nationwide protests in France on Saturday has been marked by violent clashes between demonstrators and police as several hundred thousand people are expected to march throughout the country. Media reported incidents in the country’s largest cities including Lyon, Bordeaux, Marseille and Paris. Dozens of rioters clashed with law enforcement on the capital’s Place de la République, next to a much larger number of demonstrators gathered for an authorized march that started from Paris’s central square. Footage showed Lyon’s tourist board office engulfed in flames on the city’s Place Bellecour. A police station was vandalized in Marseille, where a group of “rioters” also entered city hall, Mayor Benoît Payan said. He told BFMTV that “damage was objectively fairly limited,” although the act of vandalism was “unacceptable.” The headquarters of right-wing TV channel CNews in Paris was also targeted , authorities said. Advertisement Advertisement More than 160 people had already been arrested across the country by midday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez’s office told reporters. Students, farmers and members of the Yellow Jacket movement, among others, were slated to take to the streets on Saturday in a “convergence of struggles” to protest raising living costs, sluggish wages and deep disagreements with the government. The government was expecting “a fairly large turnout,” Nuñez said on Friday. Saturday’s demonstrations originated in the student protests that began last month with school blockades and calls for better studying conditions, more teachers and more funding. The movement has since spread nationwide — and become a political issue as the campaign for next year’s presidential election heats up. The government has struggled to deal with the crisis — which Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu described as “urban violence” — and is hoping the student movement will now fade because of a two-week school holiday that started Friday evening. “The mobilization is marked by a very strong involvement of the ultra-left movement, which is only looking to cause disorder,” Nuñez’s office said Saturday, adding that the minister reiterated his “instructions of utmost firmness” to local prefects and police forces. Advertisement Advertisement The government has defended the law enforcement response to the student protests despite numerous allegations of police brutality, including incidents that left one teenager with a severed hand and another blind in one eye. Nuñez said the use of “stun grenades” was authorized on Saturday, after a temporary ban on their use against students. While far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon is backing protesters, far-right leader Jordan Bardella pledged support for the police. Mélenchon criticized the media for only showing violent clashes while “everything is proceeding peacefully, with tens of thousands of people calmly taking part.” However, Bardella said on Saturday that protests were only made up of “chaos professionals,” adding: “As we said, working France, which is taking the full brunt of inflation and cost-of-living struggles, did not take to the streets today.” The police and protesters clashed in other European countries on Saturday, too. A student-led protest against corruption and unemployment in Albania’s capital Tirana reportedly turned violent , so did another one in Brussels. This is a developing story. Victor Goury-Laffont contributed reporting. Advertisement Advertisement

Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: Global Microsoft outage chaos as tech firm says there are ‘signs of stabilisation’ Users of Microsoft Teams and Outlook in businesses and public services reporting problems. Plus would you like to spend time as a helpful furry little post delivery service? Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Martin Belam Fri 13 Nov 2026 07.16 EST Last modified on Fri 13 Nov 2026 08.25 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. A global outage of vital Microsoft systems has crippled businesses and public services around the world. The tech company said it was seeing “early signs of stabilisation” after the failure affected millions of users for more than 12 hours on Thursday and Friday. Some but not all users were reporting problems with services including Microsoft Teams and Outlook email. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, and more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies use Copilot, Microsoft’s AI chatbot, according to the company. Microsoft said that there were no indications that the outage had been caused by a cyber-attack. We are covering the recovery efforts and continuing impact in this live blog . US commerce secretary under pressure over Nvidia View image in fullscreen Alice Huang (right) attending a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang (left). Photograph: CTI/AFPTV/AFP/Getty Images One of Donald Trump’s top lieutenants could reportedly soon be fired , as criticism mounts over the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick’s apparent lack of action over the Nvidia spying scandal. Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday , and was replaced on an interim basis by the chief financial officer, Colette Kress, after reports emerged of his multiple affairs, most importantly with Alice Huang (no relation), who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Who are the main people involved? For more information on the cast of characters, Dan Milmo has this profile of outgoing Huang , who went from washing dishes at Denny’s to becoming the rock star of AI, and Dara Kerr has this piece answering the question: who is Colette Kress ? And yesterday my newsletter colleague Hettie O’Brien had this excellent breakdown of what we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang . We also have this timeline of how the scandal unfolded . Fatal Brooklyn building collapse devastates community View image in fullscreen Workers at the scene of a partial building collapse. Photograph: Ryan Murphy/Getty Images New York officials have confirmed at least eight deaths , six adults and two children, in the collapse of a building in Flatbush, New York. At least 18 people have sustained non-fatal but serious injuries. Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, confirmed officials were working with the department of buildings to investigate 100 other sites in the city with connections to the building that gave way. Red Cross set up a supply center at the Flatbush YMCA down the street from the collapse, providing temporary housing, social services and mental health support. “The last time I saw something like this was when I went to work at 9/11,” one witness said . Trump says no deal needed on Iran war and orders Vance to focus on domestic issues View image in fullscreen Donald Trump and JD Vance on Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery. Photograph: Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images In an apparent snub to the vice-president, who had been closely linked to negotiations with Tehran, Trump has said that the US is no longer seeking a deal to end the war with Iran and ordered JD Vance to focus on domestic politics instead. Vance last week blamed the conflict for the historic rout dealt to Republicans in the midterm elections. What is the latest on terrorist threats to US bases in Britain? A suspect held in a New York jail, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, has been linked to an alleged handler behind Iran-linked operations in Britain , including what was suspected to be an attempted attack on US forces stationed at RAF Fairford. How has Pete Hegseth reacted to being reprimanded by a guard? After video of the defense secretary and his aides being admonished by a guard near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier went viral, Hegseth has awarded a Joint Service Commendation Medal to the soldier who called him out, saying: “We love standards. Well done.” In other news … View image in fullscreen Dan Hicks in 2023. Photograph: Ben Jared/PGA TOUR Dan Hicks, NBC’s voice of golf and Olympic swimming, has died a ged 64 . His wife, the ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, said: “Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan.” Hicks enjoyed a 35-year career at NBC Sports. Family Dollar is to pay $63m to settle overcharging allegations . The settlement with the FTC and state officials comes after the Guardian’s exposé of its pricing practices. The father of a South Carolina baby who survived being buried alive has been charged with attempted murder . The child was found crying and covered in dirt in a dog crate by rescuers after being left there for about 24 hours. Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi , the prediction market company has said. Michael Carrick has been sacked at Manchester United, and will be replaced by Mauricio Pochettino. The Argentinian will lead the USMNT for the last times in their two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti. Stat of the day: Darth Vader’s lightsaber sells for nearly $5m View image in fullscreen David Prowse and Mark Hamill in Star Wars: Return of the Jedi. Photograph: Landmark Media/Alamy In a case of “may the force be with your bank account”, Darth Vader’s lightsaber prop from The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi sold for $4.875m . Culture Pick: A relaxing game and some jaw-dropping documentaries View image in fullscreen Tanuki: Pon’s Summer video game screenshot Photograph: Denkiworks The impending violence, mayhem and boisterous satire of GTA6 may by the focus of the video game industry right now, but Christian Donlan reviews Tanuki: Pon’s Summer , a multi-platform release in which an adorable raccoon mends the world, one parcel at a time. It sounds very soothing. If you fancy watching something with a bit more bite though, Phil Hoad has this list of the 20 most shocking and affecting true stories ever committed to cinema. Don’t miss this: The sinister power of Friday 13th – how this maligned date affects our lives View image in fullscreen Friday 13th illustration. Composite: Guardian Design Are you superstitious? Leah Harper looks at the origins of some of the worries around Friday 13th, and finds there are some real-world impacts, as it is a day with lower flight fares, fewer weddings and even an impact on property prices. … or this: Farewell, Cybertruck: why the winding down of the ‘Maga hat on wheels’ is a sign of the times View image in fullscreen A Cybertruck in a lake in Texas. Photograph: Grapevine Police Department Eccentric and overhyped, Tesla’s Cybertruck became a stand-in for Elon Musk during his ascent in the Republican party. Matthew Cantor says it will join the ranks of other vehicles symbolic of their eras. … or this either: The final minute of the SS United States above water View image in fullscreen The SS United States sinks. Photograph: Destin-Fort Walton Beach, Florida The historic ship will rest on the seafloor as an artificial reef at a depth of approximately 180ft. This video shows the moment it was sunk below the waves . Climate check: World is now in ‘age of electricity’, energy agency chief says View image in fullscreen A man charging an electric car near Damascus. Photograph: Louai Beshara/AFP/Getty Images Fiona Harvey is in Antalya for the Guardian at Cop31, and in this exclusive she spoke to Fatih Birol , the executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA). He told her that more than twice as much electricity generation would be added to the global economy in the next decade as in the last, as countries scramble to secure their energy supplies against fossil fuel price volatility and supply shocks.
